findings.title: 60 of 72 records carry template/placeholder 'heritage evidence' (water CAS, Matrix-#HEX formulas, generic manuscript, grid coordinates, generic UNESCO label) presented as authentic in UI and exports
findings.confidence: high on facts (counts reproduced by A00, W1 and A15); medium-high on the severity choice. Critical is scoped to the source-citable cultural-reference claim (verdict 2); for the design-toolkit claim the same facts weigh High
locations: heritage-data.ts geoSpatial.coordinates: six points lat 32.4279+0.5i / lng 53.688+0.3i reused by 60 colors
heritage-data.ts historicalManuscriptRef: 'رسالات کهن رنگرزی سنتی و صنعتی ایران زمین' x60
heritage-data.ts chemicalFormula 'Natural Organic / Mineral Complex (Matrix #HEX)' x54
app/template.html:1113 'نام کانی‌شناسی اصیل', :1139 'رساله کهن خطی و سند تاریخی مرجع', :1366 static 'موزه هنرهای اسلامی' badge
packages/core/tokens/w3c-tokens.json and style-dictionary.json (120 occurrences each of the water CAS)
findings.observed: CAS 7732-18-5 is water (H2O). In 54/54 template records the 'formula' embeds the record's own HEX value. Coordinates are an arithmetic grid (e.g. 54.288000000000004). The dossier shows the placeholder formula, mineral name, manuscript, crystal system and UNESCO label under labels meaning 'authentic' and 'reference historical manuscript', and a static museum badge appears on every color. The CAS number itself is not rendered in the dossier (app.js has 0 casNumber references); it reaches users through the DTCG/JSON downloads, the evidence tab's W3C token view (app.js:822) and the npm tokens/ files. palettes.ts:57 also copies the placeholder manuscript into provenance.historicalReference.citation.
findings.expected: Heritage fields either cite a locatable source for the specific claim, or are empty and labeled 'no source recorded'. Placeholders must never be labeled authentic or exported as data (audit brief §4C/§4D; do not fabricate).
findings.reproduction: grep -c '7732-18-5 (Authentic Historical Specimen)' packages/core/src/tokens/heritage-data.ts -> 120; grep -c 7732-18-5 packages/core/tokens/w3c-tokens.json -> 120; grep -o '"lat": [0-9.]*' heritage-data.ts | sort | uniq -c (six values x10); open the evidence dialog for any color to see the labels.
findings.impact: Critical-threshold justification (A15 four-part test): pervasive (60/72 records, every evidence dimension; the other 12 have no located citation); central (the evidence dossier is presented as the product's provenance layer); asserted at the point of use (labels, static badges, and the EN 'Primary source documented' banner); and propagated (exports, including the placeholder as a 'citation'). Mitigation: heritageStatus='unverified' on 72/72 and honest README.fa/DESIGN_SYSTEM text. But 'unverified' names the wrong kind of uncertainty: these values are known-false or non-referential, not unchecked citations.
findings.scope: 60/72 colors in 10/12 palettes (all except isfahan-tiles; achaemenid-majesty has the water CAS but specific other fields).
findings.recommended_fix: Replace the placeholder values with null plus status 'no-source' in the data. Remove the 'اصیل' and 'سند تاریخی مرجع' labels and the static museum badge. Show 'no source recorded' in the UI. Keep the stable IDs.
findings.acceptance_test: grep for 7732-18-5, 'Matrix #', the generic manuscript phrase and the six grid latitudes returns 0 in src, tokens and HTML. Every displayed heritage field either has a source ID or shows 'no source recorded'.
findings.dependencies_effort_uncertainty: 0.5-1.5 days engineering; no research needed to remove. Re-populating the fields needs archive/museum research (backlog).
findings.independent_review: A15 confirmed; counts exact (60 records, 120 CAS occurrences in src, w3c, SD, HTML and a fresh export; 54/54 self-HEX formulas; 60 grid points). Correction applied: CAS not rendered in the UI. Upgraded to Critical for verdict 2, with High as the floor.

findings.title: @persian-palette/core declares license 'MIT' but hard-depends on and bundles apca-w3 (Limited W3 License: web content only, commercial use needs a signed agreement); its dependency colorparsley (AGPL-3.0) is loaded at runtime by ESM consumers
findings.confidence: high on the facts; legal consequence needs counsel
findings.observed: package.json says 'MIT'. The CJS bundle contains apca-w3 and MCU code. ESM consumers install and evaluate colorparsley (AGPL-3.0), although its functions are never called.
findings.expected: The license metadata must describe what is distributed. APCA-W3 terms restrict scope (web content only) and prohibit commercial use without a signed agreement.
findings.reproduction: grep '// node_modules/' packages/core/dist/index.cjs; npm view apca-w3 license; W3's resolve-hook trace.
findings.impact: License scanners and SBOMs see 'MIT only'. Downstream commercial or native use may conflict with the APCA-W3 terms.
findings.scope: Every consumer of the npm tarball; the HTML studio also bundles apca-w3.
findings.recommended_fix: Get counsel. Set a truthful SPDX expression or externalize apca-w3 from the CJS build, document the APCA terms, and consider an optional peer dependency.
findings.acceptance_test: The tarball's license metadata and README state all bundled and runtime terms; a license scanner run in a consumer lists apca-w3 and colorparsley with their real licenses.
findings.independent_review: A15 confirmed with correction: Material Color Utilities (Apache-2.0, license text shipped) removed from the headline. The blocker is the apca-w3 hard dependency plus the open AGPL question; A15 reproduced the ESM runtime load with its own resolve hook.

findings.title: Unsupported authenticity/standard wording in Persian data and UI ('اصیل', 'استاندارد جهانی', 'ثبت‌شده', 'کد رسمی', 'اصلاح شده … دقیق'), including 24 of 72 HEX values that equal modern named-color list entries
findings.confidence: high for the exact matches; medium for intent
locations: heritage-data.ts meaningFa: isfahan-tiles-c1 (:30), -c2 (:114), -c3 (:198); achaemenid-majesty-c1 (:549); behzad-miniature-c4 (:1320); persian-gulf-pearls-c1 (:3144); gardens-of-shiraz-c1 (:3663)
findings.observed: Examples: #1C39BB 'Persian Blue', #CC3333 'Persian Red', #00A693 'Persian Green', CSS #40E0D0 turquoise, #DAA520 goldenrod. Data text: 'استاندارد جهانی فیروزه‌ای ایرانی', 'اصلاح شده برای بازتاب دقیق کبالت ...'. One record admits 'معروف به Persian Green در کاتالوگ‌های جهانی'.
findings.expected: A modern list value may be used as a design choice, but it should not be presented as a heritage standard or as a measured match (audit brief §4C: separate the documented name from the exact digital match).
findings.reproduction: Compare every HEX with the W3C CSS Color 4 named colors and the Wikipedia-derived color list (W1 sources S001 and S002).
findings.impact: Designers may believe they are using historically calibrated values.
findings.scope: 24 colors; 7 of them carry 'Persian' names from modern lists.
findings.recommended_fix: Label each HEX as 'designer choice' and name its list origin where it has one ('matches CSS named color turquoise'). Remove 'world standard', 'accurate' and 'calibrated'.
findings.acceptance_test: No meaningFa or meaning string contains 'استاندارد جهانی', 'دقیق' or 'ثبت‌شده' for a designer-choice HEX; the ledger's design_status is shown in the UI.
findings.dependencies_effort_uncertainty: 2-4 hours of copy plus a data field.
findings.independent_review: A15 recounted 24/72 (5 CSS + 23 list, union 24; S002 stores some values as 3-digit hex) and 16 meaningFa strings asserting a standard/registration/correction (W1 listed 14: a lower bound). Downgraded from High to Medium: choosing a named web color is not an error; the defect is the wording. Merges former MSR-I18N-004 (superlatives).
